# 0049: Effort is the third matrix axis, and a bad rung stops the sweep before it spends

Status: accepted, 2026-09-22. Refines
[0015](0015-harness-is-the-axis-and-the-project-owns-the-matrix.md) (harness is the
axis and the project owns the matrix) with a third axis,
[0034](0034-a-harness-is-a-class-and-the-registry-is-the-only-dispatch.md) (a harness
is a class and the registry is the only dispatch) with a fourth question asked of a
harness, and
[0037](0037-the-emitted-records-are-types-and-the-cache-tree-has-one-owner.md) (the
cache tree has one owner) with a sixth coordinate that is not a sixth level. Extends
[0007](0007-unpriced-model-aborts-before-spend.md)'s stop-before-spend rule to the new
axis. Additive: `result.json` gains `effort`, `history.json` gains `effort`,
`report/index.json` gains `effort`, and every existing capture still walks, links and
replays unchanged.

## Context

Both shipped CLIs now take a reasoning budget, and it moves the two things a sweep
exists to compare: how much a cell costs and how well it does. `claude --effort
<level>` accepts `low, medium, high, xhigh, max`; codex reads
`model_reasoning_effort` from its config, which `codex exec -c` overrides. A matrix
that could only name a harness and a model could not ask the question at all --
"is opus at `low` cheaper *and* good enough here than sol at `xhigh`" is a
three-axis question, and the plugin had two axes.

The obstacle is that neither CLI fails on a rung it does not recognise. Verified
against the installed versions:

```
$ claude --effort bogus -p "hi"
Warning: Unknown --effort value 'bogus' - ignoring it and using the default
effort. Valid values: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.
```

and `codex exec -c model_reasoning_effort=bogus` launches without comment. A typo
in a matrix line therefore buys a full-priced run at the default budget, stores a
result, and the report names a rung the run never had. That is exactly the failure
0007 refuses for an unpriced model, arriving through a different door.

The vocabularies may also disagree, and neither CLI is a reliable witness to its
own. codex-cli 0.155.1's local `model_reasoning_effort` enum lists `none`,
`minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra` and `persistent`; the
gpt-5.6 models accept six of those, and the CLI validates none of it. A paid sweep
at `minimal` returned, for both models::

    Unsupported value: 'minimal' is not supported with the 'gpt-5.6-sol' model.
    Supported values are: 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'.

So a ladder read off a CLI's own enum is wrong in both directions at once: it
offers rungs the provider rejects and omits rungs the provider has. An author
naming a native rung therefore cannot know from the CLI whether the word will
survive the request.

## Decision

**A matrix entry gains an optional third component: `harness/model/effort`.** An
entry with two components is unchanged in every respect -- it leaves the CLI on
whatever default its own configuration gives it, produces the node id it always
produced, and writes to the directory it always wrote to. The absence of a rung is
a value, not a gap.

**The vocabulary is closed, and it lives in `model/effort.py`.** `Effort` is a
`StrEnum` holding every word an entry may use (ADR 0041), and a harness declares
the rungs it actually has as an ordered `Harness.efforts` ladder -- lowest first,
because the order is load-bearing. `harness/claude.py` and `harness/codex.py` each
render the rung in their own dialect (`--effort <rung>` against `-c
model_reasoning_effort=<rung>`), so nothing outside `harness/` knows either
(ADR 0034). `model/registry.py` gains the lookup, as the one declared edge from the
domain into the adapter layer (ADR 0039).

**The portable aliases `min`, `mid` and `max` name a position, not a level.** They
resolve against whichever ladder the harness has, by index, so they follow a harness
that gains or loses a rung. `max` is deliberately both an alias and a native top
rung, and resolves to itself where a harness has it. Both shipped harnesses declare
the same five rungs, so the aliases resolve identically on each today; that is a
fact about these two CLIs, not a rule the resolution depends on.

**A ladder is pinned to what the provider accepts, not to what the CLI offers.**
`Harness.efforts` is a claim about the request surviving, so a rung goes in only
when it has been seen to work, and a rung the provider rejects comes out. `none` is
accepted by codex and still omitted: it disables reasoning rather than setting a
budget, so it would put a no-reasoning cell in every default sweep.

**Resolution happens once, at matrix expansion, and an unresolvable rung is an
error there.** `mx.expand` turns the typed word into a native rung before a `Cell`
exists, so the node id, the evidence directory and the report row all carry what
was actually sent rather than what was typed. A word outside the vocabulary, a rung
this harness does not have, or a fourth component stops collection with the
offending line named -- before any cell has spent anything, which is the only
moment at which refusing is free.

**Effort is a sixth coordinate but not a sixth level.** The evidence tree is a
published contract: the report page fetches
`../results/{skill}/{harness}/{model}/{run}/{session}/log.jsonl` by that exact
shape. So the rung rides the model's level as `{model}--{effort}`, owned by
`model/layout.py` like every other name under the cache root (ADR 0037). A level
with no separator named no effort, which is precisely what every capture written
before this record holds -- so the glob, the links and the replay are all unchanged
and no migration exists to forget to run.

**The rung is attached by the derivation pipeline, not folded by a harness.** No
session log records what a CLI was *asked* for, only what it then did; a harness
that folded the rung would be reporting its own argv back to itself. `RunResult`
gains `effort` alongside `case` and `skill_coverage`, set by `runtime/pipeline.py`
from the cell that ran, and carried forward from the stored result on a replay --
so a rebuild reports the effort the run had rather than the effort today's matrix
would give it.

## Consequences

Three emitted documents gain one key each: `result.json`, `history.json` and
`report/index.json` all carry `effort` (empty or null when the cell named none),
mirrored in `report-ui/src/lib/types.ts` and the shipped glossary. The
characterization goldens move by that key alone and no measured value in them
changes, which is the evidence that this adds a coordinate rather than
redistributing one.

`--effort` narrows a sweep the way `--harness` and `--model` do, and matches the
*resolved* rung -- so `--effort mid` selects whatever `mid` meant on each harness,
which is the only reading under which one flag narrows both arms of a two-harness
sweep to the same intensity. A word that resolves on one harness and not another
simply does not match the other's cells: narrowing a sweep is not the moment to
refuse a flag, because nothing is about to be billed.

Two cells of one case may now differ in nothing but their rung, so the build
workspace name includes it; without that the pair would overwrite each other.

The first paid sweep across the axis (20 cells, one case, both harnesses) paid for
itself by falsifying the ladder this record was first written with. `minimal` was
declared a codex rung and is not one; `max` was withheld as unverifiable and is one.
Both `minimal` cells exited 1 having produced nothing, and `check_run_is_real`
failed them rather than grading an empty run -- which is the evidence gate of
ADR 0002 doing exactly its job, on the first axis value that needed it.

That is the argument for validating at expansion rather than trusting the flag,
restated as data: the CLI forwarded a word it listed in its own enum, and the
request died at the provider. A ladder is a claim about the request surviving, and
only a run can settle it. Adding or removing a rung is one tuple entry, and it moves
what `mid` resolves to, which is why the ladder is ordered rather than a set.

## Lens

An axis is only an axis once a wrong value on it can fail. A knob that every
consumer accepts and silently ignores is not a parameter, it is a comment: the
sweep spends full price and reports a number that names a setting it never had. So
the vocabulary closes where the plugin can still refuse, and the word the author
typed is resolved into the word the CLI received before anything downstream stores
it -- because a record that keeps the typed word cannot say what was measured.
